java_locations.role: Stores an explicit floating-note command color as the entity BACK override and leaves BACK unset when the command omits color.
Parses attached-note colors, applies note stereotype colors to missing channels, and stores the resulting Colors on the generated NOTE entity.
Resolves every NOTE through the merged note style; entity BACK wins when present, otherwise PName.BackGroundColor from the style supplies the fill.
Maps DESCRIPTION diagrams to the componentDiagram style family used by EntityImageNote.
Migrates noteBackgroundColor to the note style's BackGroundColor property, so omitted-color notes inherit it through normal style resolution.

rust_locations.role: Already preserves explicit colors for inline and multiline floating and attached note forms; parsing is no longer the divergence.
Already maps noteBackgroundColor into the shared effective Theme.note.background used by other diagram families.
Uses an explicit note color when present but bypasses the effective theme and falls directly to a deployment-local #FEFFDD for omitted colors; both body and fold consume that wrong fallback.
The non-replay oracle painter also hardcodes the same fill for body and fold instead of consuming the resolved DESCRIPTION note style.
Demonstrates the existing shared precedence shape in another family: explicit note color first, noteBackgroundColor second.

claimed_invariant: DESCRIPTION note background is a style-cascade result, not a deployment constant. Explicit command BACK wins. For attached notes, a stereotype-specific note BACK fills a missing explicit channel next. Otherwise the effective root.element.componentDiagram.note background applies, including noteBackgroundColor and note style blocks, with the built-in note style as the final default. Body and folded corner consume one resolved fill.
causal_divergence: Rust's parser now retains explicit note colors and the top-level render pipeline already folds skinparams into Theme.note.background. Deployment painting ignores that effective theme: deployment_note_fill selects note.color and otherwise returns the local NOTE_FILL literal. Explicit-color held-outs therefore pass while every omitted-color style override falls back to #FEFFDD. The error is an unwired style-cascade handoff shared by floating and attached painters, not separate command grammar defects.
planned_model_change: Create one DESCRIPTION note-background resolver that accepts the effective Theme and a DeploymentNote. Resolve explicit note.color first, then the effective note style background, whose default remains the source-provenanced built-in note color. Pass that resolved fill into both no-oracle note painters and the non-replay oracle note painter so body and fold cannot diverge. Preserve note geometry, ownership, layout, source order, and connector construction. Treat stereotype-specific attached-note color as a separate parser/style extension if the current AST cannot yet represent it, and keep a fresh failing perturbation rather than pretending generic style support covers it.
perturbation_axes: generic noteBackgroundColor versus note style block
acceptance: Omitted-color floating and attached DESCRIPTION notes consume the effective note background style in both inline and multiline forms.
Explicit named and hex command colors continue to override noteBackgroundColor.
Body and folded corner always use the same resolved fill.
Generic and block-form note style perturbations pass; unsupported stereotype residue, if any, stays preserved and declared.
Existing parser/renderer tests and no-oracle ratchets remain green.
An independent checker attacks command form, precedence, style syntax, stereotypes, ownership, and fold consistency at the exact implementation revision.
forbidden_approaches: changing the deployment-local fallback literal to the held-out color
parsing skinparams again inside individual note painters
styling body and fold through separate branches
changing geometry, ownership, Magma, or connector coordinates for a color mismatch
fixture labels, expected colors keyed to text, comparator changes, or baseline changes
constant_provenance: The final default remains Java's merged built-in note style; the existing #FEFFDD value may remain only as the Theme.note default or a source-cited equivalent. NOTE_FOLD, margins, connector dimensions, and stroke widths are outside this mechanism and must not change without separate Java citations.
